graders.name: overview-not-invented
graders.evidence:
# Overview

## What this is

A Terraform configuration (`aws` provider only) with two child modules called from the
root: `modules/network` and `modules/app` (`main.tf:14-20`). There is no README, package
manifest, or other repo metadata naming the project — `system` below is the kit's
directory-derived id, not a name declared anywhere in the checkout.

## Context

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  operator["Operator (human)"] -->|"runs terraform plan / apply"| system["system\n(this Terraform configuration)"]
  system -->|"provisions resources via the aws provider"| aws["AWS (external)"]
```

- `operator` and `aws` are the only context-level parties evidenced by the code: a human
  invokes Terraform, and the `aws` provider block (`main.tf:2-12`) talks to AWS. No CI
  system, remote git host, log sink, or workspace/state backend is declared anywhere in
  the checkout, so none of those are modelled — see Unknowns below.
- `docs/architecture/model/hand.c4` carries this same context as a LikeC4 model; a
  rendered PNG could not be produced in this environment (see Unknowns).

## Containers / modules

The root module (`main.tf`) calls two child modules and does nothing else:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  root["root (main.tf)"] --> network["modules/network"]
  root["root (main.tf)"] --> app["modules/app"]
  network -->|"aws_vpc.main"| aws["AWS"]
  app -->|"aws_instance.web, aws_instance.worker"| aws
```

| module | source | calls from | resources it declares |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| network | `./modules/network` | `main.tf` | `aws_vpc.main` (`modules/network/main.tf:1-3`) |
| app | `./modules/app` | `main.tf` | `aws_instance.web`, `aws_instance.worker` (`modules/app/main.tf:1-9`) |

The full module/provider/resource inventory (generated, not hand-written) is at
`docs/reference/infra.md`. The component/import graph at `docs/reference/components.md`
is empty by design: the fold-rules scan (`docs/architecture/fold-rules.json`) targets
`modules/`, and Terraform module calls are not import statements the generic scanner
resolves — the Terraform-specific graph in `infra.md` is the authoritative one for this
repo.

Note: `modules/network` and `modules/app` are both called from root but nothing in
either module's code references the other — `modules/app/main.tf` has no
`vpc_security_group_ids`, `subnet_id`, or any input wired from `modules/network`'s VPC,
and `modules/network/main.tf` declares no `output` block a caller could consume. As
written, the two modules do not compose; see `docs/architecture/risks.md`.

## Providers

One provider, evidenced at `main.tf:1-12`:

| name | source | version constraint | configured in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aws | hashicorp/aws | ~> 5.0 | `main.tf:10-12` (`region = "us-east-1"`) |

Neither child module declares its own `terraform`/`required_providers` block; both
inherit the root's `aws` provider (standard Terraform behavior for a provider passed
implicitly to child modules with no `providers = {}` argument at the call site).

## Resource inventory

Generated from the checkout at `docs/reference/infra.md`; summarized here:

| type | count | where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| aws_vpc | 1 | `modules/network/main.tf:1-3` |
| aws_instance | 2 | `modules/app/main.tf:1-9` |

No other resource types, data sources, or provisioners appear anywhere in the checkout.

## Unknowns (GAP)

- GAP: no rendered C4 view. LikeC4 rendering needs `npx` to fetch the `likec4` package;
  this environment's sandbox denied `registry.npmjs.org` (`docs/architecture/_run/run.md`),
  so the context view image was not produced. The `hand.c4`/`generated.c4` model text is
  present and should render once network access to the npm registry is available.
- GAP: no remote state backend is declared (no `backend` block in `main.tf`), so where
  Terraform state is actually stored when this is run is not shown by the code.
- GAP: no CI/CD pipeline exists in the checkout (no `.github/workflows`, no other CI
  config found) — `docs/reference/delivery.md` is correctly empty, not a GAP in the
  extractor, but the required "pipeline" view has nothing to show either.
- GAP: no documented architecture decisions exist (no `docs/decisions/` or `docs/adr/` in
  the checkout), so no ADR index could be generated without inventing a decision that was
  never recorded.
- GAP: the AWS credentials used when `terraform apply` runs are not shown by the code —
  see `docs/architecture/secrets.md`.
- GAP: no owner, maintainer, or contact is recorded anywhere in the checkout (no README,
  CODEOWNERS, or similar).
